items.title: Haywood Hillyer Interview, 1958-05-04
items.q: I think it, that probably was the Dixie Lane Jazz Band now, don't you think?

ctx.x: No, I don't know what band it was, but... It was the Halfway House. The Halfway House, and I think it, that probably was the Dixie Lane Jazz Band now, don't you think? It's called the Halfway House Orchestra. It's called the Halfway House Orchestra. And the children thought it was wonderful. I thought it was... All this jazz was dreadful and I still did. Tell her yes. I'll ring her up later. Tell her here. And, uh, where was I? Oh, yes.
You were saying that it was horrible.

items.title: Haywood Hillyer Interview, 1958-05-14
items.q: The interviewee discusses 'Dixie Lane jazz' as a genre/style of music ('It was mostly Dixie Lane jazz that we... We did our music to'), not as a specific person named Dixie Lane.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. What's that, you and your friends? My friends.

Well, I... All of them together are very fond of jazz. We... In fact, we hit a band a few years ago that we thought a great deal of. We played for different parties and different yacht club dances and affairs like that. In fact, we made a few recordings. Mm-hmm. It was mostly Dixie Lane jazz that we... Uh-huh. We did our music to. That's modern jazz in any way.

Yeah. Well, that's what I'm talking about. That's the subject between Dixie Lane jazz, of course. Uh-huh. Uh... Have you noticed, uh, using jazz bands at parties? Uh, uh, to, uh, most of the parties you tend to go to hire jazz bands. So, I'm sorry.
